summary: The customer wants to assess the feasibility of fiber-based spectroscopic monitoring in a tablet press feed frame to track API concentration changes in real time.

facts_stated.text: The company manufactures tablets from a powder blend comprising an API and excipients.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: We manufacture tablets from a powder blend containing an active pharmaceutical ingredient and excipients.

facts_stated.text: Laboratory analysis currently confirms whether the blend meets target specifications.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: Laboratory checks tell us whether the blend is on target

facts_stated.text: Lab test results are received with a delay, after material has already processed through the tablet press.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: results arrive after the material has moved through the press.

facts_stated.text: The initial project phase will be a pilot study comparing candidate measurement options.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: Our first pilot should compare reasonable measurement options before we commit to production equipment.

targets.purpose: follow API concentration changes in-line during tableting

heterogeneous.enquiry_quote: powder blend containing an active pharmaceutical ingredient and excipients

customer_premises.claim: A fiber-based measurement interface can be reliably installed and operated within the moving powder environment of a feed frame.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: a fiber based measurement in the feed frame could follow API concentration changes

unknowns: Identity, chemical structure, and nominal concentration/dynamic range of the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API)
Chemical nature, particle sizes, and spectral characteristics of the excipients
Specific feed frame model, paddle design, optical clearance, and available probe mounting ports/windows
Potential window fouling, powder coating, or caking behavior at the measurement interface
Required measurement frequency, sampling volume, and response time relative to feed frame residence time
Analytical performance requirements (precision, accuracy, limits of detection/quantification)
Specific laboratory reference method used (e.g., HPLC, UV-Vis) and its associated error
